This vignette demonstrates how to remove ambient RNA from a Seurat object with
Decant. If you use Decant, please cite:

> *Decant: benchmark-first ambient RNA decontamination for single-cell RNA-seq*
>
> Kushal Raj Roy
>
> R package, 2026
>
> GitHub: https://github.com/kroy3/Decant
>
> Documentation: https://decant.readthedocs.io

# Overview

In droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq, every droplet also captures some
cell-free ("ambient") RNA released by lysed cells. Each cell's counts are a
mixture of its own transcripts and this soup, so marker genes of abundant
cell types leak into all the others. Decant measures the soup from the empty
droplets of the raw (unfiltered) matrix, estimates the contamination fraction
of each cell from genes its cluster does not express, and removes ambient
counts from each cell.

Two properties matter for downstream use:

* the corrected counts never exceed the raw counts and are never negative:
  correction only removes counts, it cannot create expression;
* counts too high to be ambient (for example in doublets or rare high
  expressers) are kept rather than removed.

Decant needs the raw droplet matrix (Cell Ranger's `raw_feature_bc_matrix`)
in addition to the filtered cells.

# Load data

We use the 10x Genomics 1k PBMC dataset (v3 chemistry), which provides both
the filtered and the raw feature-barcode matrices.

```{r packages}
library(Seurat)
library(Decant)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r download}
base <- "https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v3/pbmc_1k_v3_"
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc_1k_v3")
for (which in c("filtered", "raw")) {
  tgz <- file.path(dir, paste0(which, ".tar.gz"))
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  if (!file.exists(tgz)) {
    download.file(paste0(base, which, "_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"), tgz, mode = "wb")
  }
  untar(tgz, exdir = dir)
}
filtered_dir <- file.path(dir, "filtered_feature_bc_matrix")
raw_dir <- file.path(dir, "raw_feature_bc_matrix")
```

# Standard Seurat processing

Decant uses the object's cluster identities to estimate contamination, so we
first cluster the cells as usual.

```{r seurat}
pbmc <- CreateSeuratObject(Read10X(filtered_dir), min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
pbmc <- subset(pbmc, subset = nFeature_RNA < 5000)
pbmc <- NormalizeData(pbmc)
pbmc <- FindVariableFeatures(pbmc)
pbmc <- ScaleData(pbmc)
pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:15)
pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, resolution = 0.5)
pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:15)
```

```{r umap, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
DimPlot(pbmc, label = TRUE) + NoLegend()
```

# Run Decant

`RunDecant()` reads the raw matrix, takes the droplets with 1 to 100 UMIs as
the soup, estimates each cell's contamination fraction and writes the
corrected counts to a new assay, `Decant`.

```{r run_decant}
pbmc <- RunDecant(pbmc, raw = raw_dir)
pbmc
```

Each cell's estimated contamination fraction is stored in `decant_rho`:

```{r rho}
summary(pbmc$decant_rho)
```

```{r rho_plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
VlnPlot(pbmc, features = "decant_rho", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()
```

This is a clean sample: the median cell has well under 1% ambient RNA.

Per-cluster diagnostics are stored in the object's `Misc` slot. A cluster
flagged `low_power` has too few genes that it clearly does not express (and
that are abundant enough in the soup) to estimate its own contamination; it
borrows the evidence-weighted value of the clusters that do. With low
contamination and closely related immune cell types, as here, most clusters
borrow.

```{r diagnostics}
diag <- Misc(pbmc, "decant")$rho_diagnostics
diag[, c("cluster", "n_cells", "rho", "n_absent_genes", "low_power", "borrowed")]
```

# Effect of the correction

The monocyte marker *LYZ* is one of the most abundant genes in the soup. Its
mean count per cell, by cluster, before and after correction: the small
ambient counts in the other clusters are removed, while the monocyte
clusters keep nearly all of theirs.

```{r lyz, fig.height=4}
lyz <- data.frame(
  cluster = Idents(pbmc),
  raw = FetchData(pbmc, vars = "rna_LYZ", layer = "counts")[, 1],
  decant = FetchData(pbmc, vars = "decant_LYZ", layer = "counts")[, 1]
)
aggregate(cbind(raw, decant) ~ cluster, data = lyz, FUN = mean)
```

```{r lyz_plot, fig.height=4}
VlnPlot(pbmc, features = c("rna_LYZ", "decant_LYZ"), layer = "counts", pt.size = 0, ncol = 2)
```

Correction only removes counts:

```{r bounds}
raw_counts <- LayerData(pbmc, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
dec_counts <- LayerData(pbmc, assay = "Decant", layer = "counts")
c(min = min(dec_counts), above_raw = sum(dec_counts > raw_counts),
  share_removed = 1 - sum(dec_counts) / sum(raw_counts))
```

# Downstream analysis

The `Decant` assay holds counts; normalize it before use, and use it as the
default assay for marker detection or differential expression.

```{r downstream}
pbmc <- NormalizeData(pbmc, assay = "Decant")
DefaultAssay(pbmc) <- "Decant"
markers <- FindMarkers(pbmc, ident.1 = levels(Idents(pbmc))[1], max.cells.per.ident = 200)
head(markers)
```

# Notes and limitations

* Decant's contamination estimate relies on genes that a cluster does not
  express. In a sample of a single cell type, or when the soup closely
  resembles every cluster, contamination cannot be estimated from the counts;
  Decant warns, and a value from an independent source can be supplied with
  `RunDecant(pbmc, raw = raw_dir, rho = ...)`.
* Benchmarks against SoupX, DecontX and CellBender, including the cases where
  Decant removes less ambient RNA than DecontX, are documented at
  https://github.com/kroy3/Decant/blob/main/validation/BENCHMARK.md.
* For several samples, pass a named list of raw matrices and the meta.data
  column naming each cell's sample:
  `RunDecant(obj, raw = list(s1 = dir1, s2 = dir2), sample_col = "sample")`.
